content: ZIAGEN is the trade name for abacavir sulfate, a synthetic carbocyclic nucleoside analogue that exhibits inhibitory activity against HIV-1. The chemical name of abacavir sulfate is (1S, cis)-4-[2-amino-6-(cyclopropylamino)-9H-purin-9-yl]-2-cyclopentene-1-methanol sulfate (salt) (2:1). The compound exists as an enantiomer with an absolute configuration of 1S, 4R on the cyclopentene ring. Its molecular formula is (C14H18N6O)2H2SO4, and it has a molecular weight of 670.76 daltons. Abacavir sulfate appears as a white to off-white solid and demonstrates a solubility of approximately 77 mg/mL in distilled water at 25°C. The compound has an octanol/water partition coefficient (log P) of approximately 1.20 at a pH range of 7.1 to 7.3 and a temperature of 25°C. ZIAGEN is available in two formulations for oral administration: tablets and an oral solution. Each ZIAGEN tablet contains abacavir sulfate equivalent to 300 mg of abacavir as the active ingredient. The inactive components of the tablet include colloidal silicon dioxide, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, and sodium starch glycolate. The tablets are coated with a film composed of hypromellose, polysorbate 80, synthetic yellow iron oxide, titanium dioxide, and triacetin. The ZIAGEN Oral Solution is a liquid formulation, with each milliliter (1 mL) containing abacavir sulfate equivalent to 20 mg of abacavir (i.e., 20 mg/mL) as the active ingredient. The inactive ingredients in the oral solution include artificial strawberry and banana flavors, citric acid (anhydrous), methylparaben and propylparaben (used as preservatives), propylene glycol, saccharin sodium, sodium citrate (dihydrate), sorbitol solution, and water. Once administered, abacavir sulfate dissociates in vivo to release its free base, abacavir. All dosages of ZIAGEN are expressed in terms of the active compound, abacavir.
